atlas-gb.0168: Financial and related professional services account for over 2.4 million jobs in Great Britain, two thirds of them outside London, and the UK was the world’s largest net exporter of financial services in 2024 (£92.6 billion).
atlas-gb.0169: The UK hires graduates through structured schemes that open almost a year ahead: an online application, tests, a video interview and an assessment day, often in person. Large employers fill a share of these places from their own summer interns first.
atlas-gb.0170: Applying is open to anyone, but the timetable, not the CV, is where most Europeans lose.
atlas-gb.0172: Applications open from July to October and close when full, in order of arrival, for jobs that start the next September. Employers received 140 applications per graduate vacancy in 2025, a record, and ISE members cut graduate hiring by 8% in a year.
atlas-gb.0173: This is the ranked first route because it is where the volume is: the 100 leading graduate employers still plan graduate intakes of their own,. The Big Four alone took about 5,400 in 2024.
atlas-gb.0175: A ten-to-twelve-week internship in the penultimate summer is the main door to banks, consultancies and law firms; a good intern leaves with an offer for the following year. Competition is fierce: 101 applications per internship vacancy and 123 per undergraduate placement in 2025.
